ov: An adult male of cattle that has not been castrated. Bulls are more muscular and aggressive than cows and often have a hump on the shoulders. Most male cattle are castrated young; the few bulls kept are used for breeding, and they need careful handling.

why.dg: Bulls are more muscular and aggressive than cows.

rg: Kept on farms worldwide. Cattle were domesticated from the wild aurochs about 10,500 years ago.
df: Grass and clover; given a choice, cattle eat about 70% clover and 30% grass.

cf.tip: A bull is the uncastrated adult male; the cow is the female, and a castrated male is a steer or ox.

fx: Like most mammals, cattle are red–green colour blind.
Before 1940, being trampled, crushed or gored by a bull was one of the commonest causes of death in the dairy industry.
